questions.explanation: Dhamma Mahamatraas were officials appointed to promote and oversee aspects of Dhamma, welfare and ethical conduct among different social and religious groups.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What are Ashoka's inscriptions?

options.A: Royal proclamations engraved on rocks, pillars and cave surfaces across the empire; primary evidence for his policies, administration and conception of Dhamma

questions.explanation: Ashoka's inscriptions are royal proclamations engraved on rocks, pillars and cave surfaces across the empire. They are primary evidence for his policies, administration and conception of Dhamma.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: In which scripts were Ashoka's inscriptions written?

options.A: Most inscriptions in the subcontinent were written in Brahmi; those in the north-west used Kharosthi; some north-western inscriptions used Greek and Aramaic

questions.explanation: Most inscriptions in the subcontinent were written in Brahmi; those in the north-west used Kharosthi. Some north-western inscriptions used Greek and Aramaic.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: In which scripts were Ashoka's inscriptions written?

options.A: Most inscriptions in the subcontinent were written in Brahmi; those in the north-west used Kharosthi; some north-western inscriptions used Greek and Aramaic

questions.explanation: Most inscriptions in the subcontinent were written in Brahmi; those in the north-west used Kharosthi. Some north-western inscriptions used Greek and Aramaic.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: In which languages were Ashoka's inscriptions written?

options.A: Most were in Prakrit dialects; Greek and Aramaic versions occur in parts of the north-west

questions.explanation: Most were in Prakrit dialects. Greek and Aramaic versions occur in parts of the north-west, reflecting the region's linguistic diversity.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Who deciphered the Brahmi script of Ashoka's inscriptions?
questions.explanation: James Prinsep deciphered Brahmi in 1837, making it possible to read many of Ashoka's inscriptions and identify the ruler titled Devanampiya Piyadasi with Ashoka through corroborating evidence.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What does the title Devanampiya Piyadasi mean?

options.A: Devanampiya means 'Beloved of the Gods' and Piyadasi means 'of pleasing appearance' or 'pleasant to behold'
options.B: Devanampiya means 'King of Kings' and Piyadasi means 'Great Warrior'
options.C: Devanampiya means 'Son of God' and Piyadasi means 'Righteous King'
options.D: Devanampiya means 'Beloved of the People' and Piyadasi means 'Just Ruler'

questions.explanation: Devanampiya means 'Beloved of the Gods' and Piyadasi means 'of pleasing appearance' or 'pleasant to behold'. Ashoka used these titles in his inscriptions.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What is the importance of Major Rock Edict XIII?

options.A: It describes the Kalinga conquest, Ashoka's remorse and his preference for conquest by Dhamma

questions.explanation: Major Rock Edict XIII describes the Kalinga conquest, Ashoka's remorse and his preference for conquest by Dhamma. It is one of the most important inscriptions for understanding his change in policy.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Which Ashokan inscription mentions the names of Greek rulers?
questions.explanation: Major Rock Edict XIII names Hellenistic rulers including Antiochus and other kings, providing evidence of Ashoka's awareness of political powers beyond the north-western frontier.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What is the importance of the Bhabru or Bairat Edict?

options.A: It expresses Ashoka's reverence for the Buddha, Dhamma and Sangha and recommends certain Buddhist teachings
options.C: It records Ashoka's visit to Lumbini

questions.explanation: The Bhabru/Bairat Edict expresses Ashoka's reverence for the Buddha, Dhamma and Sangha and recommends certain Buddhist teachings. It is important evidence of his personal Buddhist commitment.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What is the significance of the Rummindei inscription?

options.A: It records Ashoka's visit to the Buddha's birthplace and his reduction of taxes for the village; crucial evidence identifying Lumbini as the Buddha's birthplace
options.C: It records Ashoka's conversion to Buddhism

questions.explanation: The Rummindei or Lumbini pillar inscription records Ashoka's visit to the Buddha's birthplace and his reduction of taxes for the village. It is crucial evidence identifying Lumbini as the Buddha's birthplace in Ashoka's time.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What is the significance of the Nigali Sagar inscription?

options.A: It records Ashoka's enlargement of the stupa of the Buddha Kanakamuni and his visit to the site
options.C: It records Ashoka's visit to Lumbini

questions.explanation: The Nigali Sagar inscription records Ashoka's enlargement of the stupa of the Buddha Kanakamuni and his visit to the site.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What is the significance of the Maski inscription?

options.A: It uses the name 'Asoka' in association with the title Devanampiya, helping establish that Piyadasi of the inscriptions was Ashoka
options.C: It records Ashoka's visit to Lumbini

questions.explanation: The Maski inscription in Karnataka uses the name 'Asoka' in association with the title Devanampiya, helping establish that Piyadasi of the inscriptions was Ashoka.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Where is the Maski inscription located?

options.A: Maski is in present-day Raichur district of Karnataka

questions.explanation: Maski is in present-day Raichur district of Karnataka. The inscription is important in the history of decipherment and identification of Ashoka.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Which Ashokan inscriptions are found in Karnataka?

options.A: Maski, Brahmagiri, Siddapur, Jatinga-Rameshwara, Nittur and Udegalom inscriptions

questions.explanation: Important examples include the Maski, Brahmagiri, Siddapur, Jatinga-Rameshwara, Nittur and Udegalom inscriptions, among others. These demonstrate the Mauryan presence and communication network in the Deccan.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What are Ashoka's Major and Minor Rock Edicts?

options.A: Major Rock Edicts are a set of fourteen principal proclamations found at several locations; Minor Rock Edicts are shorter inscriptions
options.B: Major Rock Edicts are found only in the north-west; Minor Rock Edicts are found only in the south
options.C: Major Rock Edicts are Buddhist texts; Minor Rock Edicts are Jain texts
options.D: Major Rock Edicts are in Sanskrit; Minor Rock Edicts are in Pali

questions.explanation: Major Rock Edicts are a set of fourteen principal proclamations found at several locations, with regional variations. Minor Rock Edicts are shorter inscriptions, including messages about the king's Buddhist commitment and Dhamma.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What are Ashoka's pillar edicts?

options.A: Proclamations engraved on polished stone pillars discussing Dhamma, administration, justice, welfare and moral conduct

questions.explanation: Pillar Edicts are proclamations engraved on polished stone pillars. They discuss Dhamma, administration, justice, welfare and moral conduct.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What is the Lion Capital of Sarnath?

options.A: A polished sandstone capital from an Ashokan pillar at Sarnath, featuring four lions standing back-to-back above an abacus with animal motifs and a Dharma wheel; its surviving lion capital is India's State Emblem

questions.explanation: The Lion Capital is a polished sandstone capital from an Ashokan pillar at Sarnath, featuring four lions standing back-to-back above an abacus with animal motifs and a Dharma wheel. Its surviving lion capital is India's State Emblem; the Dharma Chakra appears on the national flag.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What is the Ashoka Chakra?

options.A: The 24-spoke wheel represented at the centre of India's national flag, based on the Dharma Chakra motif associated with the Sarnath Lion Capital

questions.explanation: The Ashoka Chakra is the 24-spoke wheel represented at the centre of India's national flag. It is based on the Dharma Chakra motif associated with the Sarnath Lion Capital.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What welfare measures are associated with Ashoka?

options.A: Medical care for humans and animals, planting of medicinal herbs, wells, roadside trees, rest facilities and measures intended to reduce suffering

questions.explanation: His inscriptions refer to medical care for humans and animals, planting of medicinal herbs, wells, roadside trees, rest facilities and measures intended to reduce suffering.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: How did Ashoka promote religious tolerance?

options.A: His edicts advise respect for all sects, restraint in praising one's own tradition and criticising others, and the value of listening to and learning from other religious communities
options.B: He banned all religions except Buddhism

questions.explanation: His edicts advise respect for all sects, restraint in praising one's own tradition and criticising others, and the value of listening to and learning from other religious communities.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What was Ashoka's contribution to Buddhism?

options.A: He supported Buddhist institutions and missions, promoted the building or enlargement of stupas according to tradition, and helped Buddhism gain wider visibility within and beyond the subcontinent
options.D: He built the first Buddhist temple

questions.explanation: Ashoka supported Buddhist institutions and missions, promoted the building or enlargement of stupas according to tradition, and helped Buddhism gain wider visibility within and beyond the subcontinent.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Did Ashoka's Dhamma abolish war or the army?

options.A: No; Ashoka expressed remorse about aggressive conquest and advocated Dhamma, but the empire retained its administrative and military structures

questions.explanation: No. Ashoka expressed remorse about aggressive conquest and advocated Dhamma, but the empire retained its administrative and military structures. His inscriptions do not announce the abolition of the army.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: When did the Gupta Empire flourish?

options.A: Early fourth century CE to sixth century CE, most powerful during the fourth and fifth centuries CE
options.B: Third century BCE to first century BCE
options.C: Sixth century BCE to fourth century BCE
options.D: Eighth century CE to tenth century CE

questions.explanation: The Gupta Empire rose in the early fourth century CE and was most powerful during the fourth and fifth centuries CE. Its political influence weakened in the sixth century CE.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Who founded the Gupta dynasty?
questions.explanation: Sri Gupta is generally regarded as the founder of the Gupta dynasty, though the empire-building phase began under Chandragupta I.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Who was Chandragupta I?

options.A: A ruler in the early fourth century CE who greatly enhanced Gupta power; his marriage to Kumaradevi of the Licchavi family strengthened the dynasty's political position
options.B: The founder of the Gupta dynasty
options.C: The ruler who defeated the Hunas
options.D: The ruler who built the Kailasa temple

questions.explanation: Chandragupta I ruled in the early fourth century CE and greatly enhanced Gupta power. His marriage to Kumaradevi of the Licchavi family strengthened the dynasty's political position.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Who was Samudragupta?

options.A: The son and successor of Chandragupta I who expanded Gupta power through campaigns; often called the 'Napoleon of India' in older historical writing
options.B: The founder of the Gupta dynasty
options.C: The ruler who defeated the Hunas
options.D: The ruler who built the Kailasa temple

questions.explanation: Samudragupta was the son and successor of Chandragupta I. He expanded Gupta power through campaigns and is often called the 'Napoleon of India' in older historical writing, a label that should be treated as a later comparison rather than a historical title.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Which inscription is the main source for Samudragupta's achievements?
questions.explanation: The Allahabad Pillar inscription, also called the Prayaga Prashasti, composed by his court poet and official Harisena, is the principal source for his campaigns and political achievements.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Who composed the Prayaga Prashasti?
questions.explanation: Harisena, a court poet and high official of Samudragupta, composed the Prayaga Prashasti in Sanskrit.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What does the Prayaga Prashasti describe?

options.A: It praises Samudragupta's conquests, political relationships with rulers of northern and southern India, frontier states and forest chiefs, and his performance of the Ashvamedha sacrifice
options.D: It describes the life of the Buddha

questions.explanation: It praises Samudragupta's conquests, political relationships with rulers of northern and southern India, frontier states and forest chiefs, and his performance of the Ashvamedha sacrifice.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What was Samudragupta's policy toward southern rulers?

options.A: The inscription describes a campaign in which southern rulers were defeated and then reinstated after submission, unlike the annexation policy followed in many northern campaigns
options.D: He formed an alliance with southern rulers

questions.explanation: The inscription describes a campaign in which southern rulers were defeated and then reinstated after submission, unlike the annexation policy followed in many northern campaigns.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Who was Chandragupta II?

options.A: Also known as Vikramaditya in later tradition, a powerful Gupta ruler who expanded influence westward and strengthened the empire
options.B: The founder of the Gupta dynasty
options.C: The ruler who defeated the Hunas
options.D: The ruler who built the Kailasa temple

questions.explanation: Chandragupta II, also known as Vikramaditya in later tradition, was a powerful Gupta ruler who expanded influence westward and strengthened the empire.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Which foreign traveller visited India during Chandragupta II's reign?
questions.explanation: The Chinese Buddhist pilgrim Faxian (Fa-Hien) travelled in India during the reign of Chandragupta II, around the early fifth century CE, to collect Buddhist texts and visit sacred sites.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What did Faxian write about India?

options.A: He described Buddhist monasteries, religious practices, social conditions and aspects of administration

questions.explanation: Faxian described Buddhist monasteries, religious practices, social conditions and aspects of administration. His account is valuable but reflects his interests as a Buddhist pilgrim and the regions he visited.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Who was Kumaragupta I?

options.A: A Gupta emperor who ruled in the fifth century CE and maintained much of the empire; later tradition associates him with the early development of Nalanda
options.B: The founder of the Gupta dynasty
options.C: The ruler who defeated the Hunas
options.D: The ruler who built the Kailasa temple

questions.explanation: Kumaragupta I was a Gupta emperor who ruled in the fifth century CE and maintained much of the empire. Later tradition associates him with the early development of Nalanda, but the precise foundation history is debated.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Who was Skandagupta?

options.A: A fifth-century Gupta ruler known for resisting the Hunas or Hepthalite groups and defending the empire during a period of growing pressure
options.B: The founder of the Gupta dynasty
options.C: The ruler who built the Kailasa temple
options.D: The ruler who defeated Pulakeshin II

questions.explanation: Skandagupta was a fifth-century Gupta ruler known for resisting the Hunas or Hepthalite groups and defending the empire during a period of growing pressure and internal strain.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What were the main sources for Gupta history?

options.A: Inscriptions, coins, seals, Sanskrit literature, Buddhist and Jain texts, foreign accounts and archaeological remains

questions.explanation: Inscriptions, coins, seals, Sanskrit literature, Buddhist and Jain texts, foreign accounts and archaeological remains are important sources.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What was the nature of Gupta administration?

options.A: The Gupta monarchy was supported by ministers, provincial governors, district and local officials, feudatory rulers and land-grant institutions; administration became more decentralised in several regions than under the Mauryas
options.B: It was highly centralised like the Mauryan administration

questions.explanation: The Gupta monarchy was supported by ministers, provincial governors, district and local officials, feudatory rulers and land-grant institutions. Administration became more decentralised in several regions than under the Mauryas.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What was the significance of land grants under the Guptas?

options.A: Land grants to Brahmanas and religious institutions expanded; such grants could transfer revenue rights and administrative privileges, contributing to changes in agrarian relations and local power
options.C: Land grants were given only to soldiers
options.D: Land grants were given only to merchants

questions.explanation: Land grants to Brahmanas and religious institutions expanded. Such grants could transfer revenue rights and administrative privileges, contributing to changes in agrarian relations and local power.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What was the economic condition under the Guptas?

options.A: Agriculture remained the main economic base, while trade, crafts, guilds and coinage continued; gold coinage was especially prominent

questions.explanation: Agriculture remained the main economic base, while trade, crafts, guilds and coinage continued. Gold coinage was especially prominent under several Gupta rulers, although its volume and quality changed over time.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What are Gupta gold coins called?
questions.explanation: Gupta gold coins are commonly called dinaras in inscriptions and numismatic discussion. They often depict rulers performing rituals, riding horses, playing instruments or engaging in martial activities.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Why is the Gupta period often called a classical age?

options.A: The period saw major achievements in Sanskrit literature, sculpture, temple architecture, mathematics, astronomy and other fields, though the label can obscure regional differences and social inequalities
options.B: It was a period of political unity
options.C: It was a period of economic prosperity
options.D: It was a period of religious tolerance

questions.explanation: The period saw major achievements in Sanskrit literature, sculpture, temple architecture, mathematics, astronomy and other fields. The label 'Golden Age' is useful as a broad cultural description but can obscure regional differences and social inequalities.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Who was Kalidasa?

options.A: A major classical Sanskrit poet and dramatist, traditionally associated with the Gupta age; works attributed to him include Abhijnanashakuntalam, Meghaduta, Raghuvamsha and Kumarasambhava

questions.explanation: Kalidasa was a major classical Sanskrit poet and dramatist, traditionally associated with the Gupta age, though his exact date and royal patronage are not certain. Works attributed to him include Abhijnanashakuntalam, Meghaduta, Raghuvamsha and Kumarasambhava.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Who wrote Aryabhatiya?
questions.explanation: Aryabhata composed the Aryabhatiya in 499 CE, a major work on mathematics and astronomy.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What were Aryabhata's important contributions?

options.A: Place-value notation, arithmetic, algebraic methods, trigonometry, approximation of pi, scientific explanation of eclipses and the statement that Earth rotates on its axis
options.D: Discovery of the circulation of blood
